greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἡνίκα ἤρξαντο οἱ ἄνθρωποι πολλοὶ γίνεσθαι ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ θυγατέρες ἐγενήθησαν αὐτοῖς.
hint: Men begin to become many, and daughters are born to them.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's first sense is *at which time, when*; *whenever* is its sense with the subjunctive.
*Began to become many*: ἄρχω with the infinitive, as at 2:3, and πολύς as the infinitive's predicate. The Hebrew is *hēḥēl lārōb*, *began to multiply*.
θυγάτηρ, *a daughter*, has one sense, so it is plain text.

reading: And [[came into being|there came to be, there arose, there was brought into existence]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[at which time|at which time, when, since, whenever]] [[began|began, made a beginning, made a beginning of, began from]] [[the men|the men, the human beings, mankind]] [[many|many, often, much and mighty and great, deep, loud, strong, large and wide, far, long]] [[to come into being|to come to be, to arise, to be brought into existence]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], and daughters [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence]] to them.

greek: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὅτι καλαί εἰσιν, ἔλαβον ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας ἀπὸ πασῶν, ὧν ἐξελέξαντο.
hint: Rahlfs's apparatus records 'angels' for 'sons' in Codex Alexandrinus.

notes.text: *The sons of God*, Hebrew *bĕnê-hāʾĕlōhîm*, word for word. [[flag]] Rahlfs's apparatus records ἄγγελοι, *angels*, for υἱοί in Codex Alexandrinus, under the siglum A^r. The same phrase returns at 6:4, where the apparatus gives no variant.
καλός, *beautiful*; the Hebrew *ṭōbōt* is *good*. καλός carries *good* only fourth, after *beautiful, beauteous, fair*.
*From all, whom they chose*: ὧν takes the case of πασῶν. ἐκλέγω, *to pick out*, in the middle *to pick out for oneself, choose out*; the entry's active glosses are left out.
*For themselves*: the reflexive, as at 3:7.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[having seen|having seen, having perceived, having beheld, having looked at]] the sons [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]] the daughters [[of the men|of the men, of the human beings, of mankind]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[beautiful|beautiful, beauteous, fair, good]] are, [[they took|they took, they received, they took hold of and grasped and seized]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — for themselves [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]], of whom [[they picked out for themselves|they picked out for themselves, they chose out, they pulled out]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεός Οὐ μὴ καταμείνῃ τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς σάρκας, ἔσονται δὲ αἱ ἡμέραι αὐτῶν ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι ἔτη.
hint: The Greek limits the saying to 'these men', and makes them flesh in the plural.

notes.text: οὐ μή with the aorist subjunctive, the strongest denial: *shall by no means stay*. καταμένω is *to stay behind, stay*, then *to remain fixed, continue*. The Hebrew verb, *yādôn*, is of uncertain sense.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bāʾādām*, *in man*, singular and without *these*. The Greek narrows the saying to *these men*.

*Because they are flesh*, διά with the articular infinitive. [[flag]] The Hebrew *bĕšaggam hûʾ bāśār* is *in their erring he is flesh*, or *since he too is flesh*; the Greek has neither, and puts σάρξ in the plural, *fleshes*.
120, as in the Hebrew.
Lower case, as at 1:2: the entry's first sense is *a blowing*, and *spirit* comes after *wind* and *breath*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] no, not [[may stay behind|may stay behind, may stay, may remain fixed, may continue]] [[the blowing|the breath, the wind, the moving air, the respiration, the spirit]] of me [[in the men|within, inside of, and by means of the men, the human beings, mankind]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the period of existence|the period of existence, the life-time and life, the age and generation, the long space of time, the era and epoch, the world]] [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of]] [[to be|to be, to exist]] them [[fleshes|fleshes, the flesh, muscles, bodies, man's nature generally]], [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], will be [[the days|the days, the day-breaks, the times]] of them a hundred twenty years.

greek: οἱ δὲ γίγαντες ἦσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ μετʼ ἐκεῖνο, ὡς ἂν εἰσεπορεύοντο οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πρὸς τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἐγεννῶσαν ἑαυτοῖς· ἐκεῖνοι ἦσαν οἱ γίγαντες οἱ ἀπʼ αἰῶνος, οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ ὀνομαστοί.
hint: Two Hebrew words, nĕpilîm and gibbōrîm, are one Greek word: giants.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has two words: *hannĕpilîm*, the Nephilim, who were on the earth, and *haggibbōrîm*, *the mighty men* of old. The Greek has γίγαντες for both. Middle Liddell's first sense is *the Giants*, *the sons of Gaia* — the mythological race — and lower case here, as the Greek has no capital.
ὡς ἄν with the imperfect, *whenever*: a repeated going in, and the imperfect ἐγεννῶσαν after it is repeated too.

The imperfect ἐγέννων, with the ending -σαν. [[flag]] The Hebrew *wĕyāldû lāhem* is *and they bore to them*: the women bear. In the Greek the sons of God stay the subject — *they begot for themselves*.

notes.lemma: οἱ ἀπʼ αἰῶνος, οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ ὀνομαστοί
notes.text: The Hebrew *mēʿôlām ʾanšê haššēm*, *of old, men of the name*. ὀνομαστός is *named*, then *of name, notable, famous*.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the giants|the giants, the sons of Gaia, the mighty]] were, and kept on being, [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]] [[in the days|within, inside of, and by means of the days, the day-breaks, the times]] [[those|those, the ones there, the more remote]] and [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[that|that, the one there, the more remote]], [[as|as, according as, considering, like]] ever [[were going into|were going into, were entering]] the sons [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] the daughters [[of the men|of the men, of the human beings, of mankind]] and [[were begetting|were begetting, were engendering, were bringing forth, were producing]] for themselves; [[those|those, the ones there, the more remote]] were, and kept on being, [[the giants|the giants, the sons of Gaia, the mighty]] the [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of period of existence|of period of existence, of life-time and life, of age and generation, of long space of time, of era and epoch, of world]], [[the men|the men, the human beings, mankind]] the [[named|named, to be named, of name and note, notable, famous]].

greek: Ἰδὼν δὲ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἐπληθύνθησαν αἱ κακίαι τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ πᾶς τις διανοεῖται ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρὰ πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας,
hint: The Hebrew's 'inclination of the thoughts' is not in the Greek.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *rabbâ rāʿat hāʾādām*, *the evil of man was great*, singular. The Greek has *the badnesses were multiplied*, in the plural. κακία is first *badness* in quality, then *cowardice*, then *moral badness, wickedness*.

notes.lemma: πᾶς τις διανοεῖται … ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρά
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕkol-yēṣer maḥšĕbōt libbô raq raʿ*, *every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil*. The Greek has *each one ponders in his heart carefully upon the evil things*: no *inclination*, no *only*, and ἐπιμελῶς, *carefully*, which the Hebrew does not have.
The adverb of ἐπιμελής, *careful, anxious about*, filed inside the adjective's entry, as ὀρθῶς is at 4:7.
πονηρός is *toilsome*, *painful*, before it is *wicked*, as at 2:9.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* alone.

greek: καὶ ἐνεθυμήθη ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἐποίησεν τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ διενοήθη.
hint: Where the Hebrew has God regret and grieve, the Greek has him ponder.

notes.text: ἐνθυμέομαι, *to lay to heart, consider well, ponder*; *to take to heart, be hurt* is its second sense. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyinnāḥem*, *and he regretted*.
διανοέομαι, *to be minded, intend*, then *to think over*. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyitʿaṣṣēb ʾel-libbô*, *and he was grieved to his heart*. The Greek has no grief and no heart.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH*; the Greek has ὁ θεός alone.

reading: and [[laid to heart|laid to heart, considered well, reflected on, pondered, thought much and deeply of, took to heart, was hurt and angry at, thought out a thing and formed a plan, inferred and concluded]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[made|fashioned, wrought, produced]] [[the man|the man, the human being, mankind]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], and [[was minded|was minded, intended, purposed, thought over, thought of, thought and supposed, was disposed]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεός Ἀπαλείψω τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ὃν ἐποίησα, ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου ἕως κτήνους καὶ ἀπὸ ἑρπετῶν ἕως τῶν πετεινῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ὅτι ἐθυμώθην ὅτι ἐποίησα αὐτούς.
hint: The Hebrew reason is 'I regret'; the Greek is 'I was angry'.

notes.text: θυμόω, *to make angry*, whose middle and passive are *to be wroth, angry*. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *kî niḥamtî*, *for I regret*. The Greek gives anger as the reason where the Hebrew gives regret, as it gave thought for regret at 6:6.
ἀπαλείφω, *to wipe off, expunge* — of a name from a register. The Hebrew *ʾemḥeh* is *I will wipe out*.
ἑρπετόν is first *a walking animal, quadruped*, and *a creeping thing, reptile* second.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[I will wipe off|I will wipe off, I will expunge, I will cancel]] [[the man|the man, the human being, mankind]], whom [[I made|I fashioned, I wrought, I produced, I performed, I did]], [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of man|of a man, of a human being]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[of flocks and herds|of flocks and herds, of a single beast, of an ox, of a sheep, of a beast for riding]] and [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of walking animals|of walking animals, of quadrupeds, of creeping things, of reptiles]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[of the winged fowl|of the winged fowl, of the birds, of the able to fly and full fledged]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[I was wroth|I was wroth, I was angry, I was wild and restive, I vented fury, I was angry with, I was angry at]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[I made|I fashioned, I wrought, I produced, I performed, I did]] them.

greek: Νωε δὲ εὗρεν χάριν ἐναντίον κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ.
hint: The Hebrew's 'in the eyes of YHWH' becomes 'before the lord God'.

notes.text: χάρις: Middle Liddell's numbered senses open with *outward grace* or *favour*, then *grace felt*, *kindness*, *thanks*. Its unnumbered heading, *Grace*, is left out, as the summaries of μετά and διά are.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʿênê YHWH*, *in the eyes of YHWH*. The Greek has no eyes, and adds τοῦ θεοῦ. ἐναντίον with the genitive is *in the presence of, before*.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.

reading: [[name:Νωε]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[found|found, found out, discovered]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[outward grace|outward grace, favour, loveliness, graciousness and kindness and goodwill, thankfulness and thanks and gratitude, a favour and kindness and boon, a gratification and delight]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]].

names.gloss: (Νωε, from Hebrew Nōaḥ, usually connected with nûaḥ, "to rest")

greek: Αὗται δὲ αἱ γενέσεις Νωε· Νωε ἄνθρωπος δίκαιος, τέλειος ὢν ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ αὐτοῦ· τῷ θεῷ εὐηρέστησεν Νωε.
hint: Noah, like Enoch, pleases God where the Hebrew has him walk with God.

notes.text: γένεσις, the word of the headings at 2:4 and 5:1, in the plural. The Hebrew *tôlĕdōt* is the same word at all three.

δίκαιος is first *observant of custom and social rule, well-ordered*, and *righteous* second; τέλειος is *having reached its end, finished, complete* before it is *perfect*. The Hebrew is *ṣaddîq tāmîm*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew *bĕdōrōtāyw* is plural, *in his generations*. Codex Alexandrinus reads γενέσει for γενεᾷ, as Rahlfs's apparatus records.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾet-hāʾĕlōhîm hithallek-nōaḥ*, *Noah walked with God*: rendered *was well pleasing to God*, as for Enoch at 5:22 and 5:24.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the origins|the origins, the sources, the productive causes, the beginnings, the manners of birth, the races and descents, the productions and generations, the creations and the created things]] of [[name:Νωε]]; [[name:Νωε]] [[man|a man, a human being]] [[observant of custom and social rule|observant of custom and social rule, well-ordered and civilised, observant of right and righteous, even and well-balanced, regular and exact, right and lawful and just, real and genuine and true, fair and moderate]], [[having reached its end|having reached its end, finished and complete, perfect and without spot or blemish, fullgrown, absolute and accomplished and perfect in his kind, fulfilled]] being [[in the race|within, inside of, and by means of the race, the stock and family, the breed, the tribe and nation, the generation, the offspring, the birth-place, the age and time of life]] of him; [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only]] [[was well pleasing|was well pleasing, seemed good, was resolved, was well pleased and satisfied]] [[name:Νωε]].

greek: ἐγέννησεν δὲ Νωε τρεῖς υἱούς, τὸν Σημ, τὸν Χαμ, τὸν Ιαφεθ.
hint: The three sons of 5:32 again, this time with the Hebrew's own 'three'.

notes.text: Here the Hebrew has *šĕlōšâ bānîm*, *three sons*, as the Greek already had at 5:32.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.

reading: [[begot|begot, engendered, brought forth, produced]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Νωε]] three sons, [[name:Σημ]], [[name:Χαμ]], [[name:Ιαφεθ]].

names.gloss: (Χαμ, from Hebrew Ḥām, usually connected with ḥam, "hot")
(Ιαφεθ, from Hebrew Yepet, which 9:27 ties to pātâ, "to make wide")

greek: ἐφθάρη δὲ ἡ γῆ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἐπλήσθη ἡ γῆ ἀδικίας.
hint: The Hebrew's violence is, in Greek, wrong-doing.

notes.text: φθείρω, *to ruin, waste, spoil, destroy*; the passive, *to go to ruin, perish*, is the entry's own gloss for this voice.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ḥāmās*, *violence*. ἀδικία is *wrong-doing, injustice*: the breach of δίκη, *right*, where the Hebrew names force.
πίμπλημι, *to fill full of*; the passive, *to be filled, become full of*, is the entry's own gloss for the voice.

reading: [[went to ruin|went to ruin, perished, was ruined, was wasted, was spoiled, was destroyed]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]], and [[was filled|was filled, became full of, was full of, had enough of]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[of wrong-doing|of wrong-doing, of injustice, of a wrong, of an injury]].

greek: καὶ εἶδεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἦν κατεφθαρμένη, ὅτι κατέφθειρεν πᾶσα σὰρξ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
hint: All flesh had ruined its way: a feminine noun with a masculine pronoun.

notes.text: *Was, having been destroyed*: the perfect participle with ἦν, a state already reached. καταφθείρω is *to destroy, spoil utterly*.
The aorist and the imperfect of φθείρω share this form. The aorist answers the Hebrew perfect *hišḥît*.
σάρξ is feminine; αὐτοῦ is not. The pronoun follows the sense, not the noun's gender. The Hebrew *darkô* agrees with *bāśār*, which is masculine.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *ʾĕlōhîm*, *God*; the Greek adds κύριος.

reading: and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], and was, and kept on being, [[having been destroyed|having been destroyed and standing destroyed, having been spoiled utterly and remaining so, having been brought to naught and remaining so]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[destroyed|destroyed, spoiled utterly, brought to naught]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[flesh|flesh, the flesh, muscles, the body, man's nature generally]] [[the way|the way, the path, the track, the road, the highway, the course, the journey, the manner and method]] of him [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Νωε Καιρὸς παντὸς ἀνθρώπου ἥκει ἐναντίον μου, ὅτι ἐπλήσθη ἡ γῆ ἀδικίας ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καταφθείρω αὐτοὺς καὶ τὴν γῆν.
hint: The Hebrew's 'end of all flesh' is, in Greek, 'the time of every man'.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *qēṣ kol-bāśār*, *the end of all flesh*. The Greek has καιρός for *end* and ἄνθρωπος for *flesh*. καιρός is first *due measure, proportion*, then *a vital part*, and of time *the right point of time, the critical time*.
ἥκω is *to have come, be present*: a present form with the sense of a perfect.
[[flag]] *ḥāmās*, *violence*, as at 6:11.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[name:Νωε]] [[due measure|due measure, proportion, fitness, a vital part, the right point of time, the proper time and season, the exact and critical time, the time, advantage and profit and fruit]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of man|of a man, of a human being]] [[has come|has come, is present, is here, has returned, has reached a point]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] of me, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[was filled|was filled, became full of, was full of, had enough of]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[of wrong-doing|of wrong-doing, of injustice, of a wrong, of an injury]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] them, and [[lo|lo, behold, see there]] I [[I destroy|I destroy, I spoil utterly, I bring to naught]] them and [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]].

greek: ποίησον οὖν σεαυτῷ κιβωτὸν ἐκ ξύλων τετραγώνων· νοσσιὰς ποιήσεις τὴν κιβωτὸν καὶ ἀσφαλτώσεις αὐτὴν ἔσωθεν καὶ ἔξωθεν τῇ ἀσφάλτῳ.
hint: The ark is a wooden box, of squared timber, with nests.

notes.text: κιβωτός, *a wooden box, chest, coffer*. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *tēbâ*, used only of this vessel and of the basket Moses is laid in. The Greek word also names the ark of the covenant, the Hebrew's *ʾărôn*: Hebrews 9:4 has τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης, and Hebrews 11:7 and 1 Peter 3:20 this one.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿăṣê-gōper*, *gopher wood*, a word found nowhere else. The Greek has *squared timbers*.
*Nests of young birds*: Middle Liddell files the word under νεοσσιά. The Hebrew *qinnîm* is also *nests*, the usual word for a bird's nest; the Greek renders it exactly.

The Hebrew *wĕkāpartā … bakkōper*, *you shall cover it with pitch*, repeats one root, and the Greek repeats one too. ἀσφαλτόω is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ gives one sense, *smear with pitch*, citing this verse, so it is plain text.
*With four equal angles, rectangular, square*: an adjective in the genitive takes *of*, as πονηρός did at 2:9.

reading: [[make|make, do, produce, create]] — one completed act seen whole, not a process observed in progress — [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore]] for yourself [[a wooden box|a wooden box, a chest, a coffer]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of woods|of woods, of firewood, of timbers, of pieces of wood, of posts, of sticks]] [[of with four equal angles|of with four equal angles, of rectangular, of square, of squared, of perfect]]; [[nests of young birds|nests of young birds, nests]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]] and you will smear with pitch it [[from within|from within, within]] and [[from without|from without, outside, without and free from]] [[with the asphalt|with the asphalt, with the bitumen]].

greek: καὶ οὕτως ποιήσεις τὴν κιβωτόν· τριακοσίων πήχεων τὸ μῆκος τῆς κιβωτοῦ καὶ πεντήκοντα πήχεων τὸ πλάτος καὶ τριάκοντα πήχεων τὸ ὕψος αὐτῆς.
hint: The cubit is, in the lexicon's first sense, the forearm.

notes.text: πῆχυς is first *the fore-arm*, and only in its fourth sense the measure, *the distance from the point of the elbow to the end of the little finger, a cubit*. The Hebrew is *ʾammâ*.
300, 50 and 30, as in the Hebrew. The numbers are plain text.

notes.lemma: τὸ μῆκος … τὸ πλάτος … τὸ ὕψος
notes.text: Three verbless clauses: *the length of the box of three hundred cubits*, and so on, with the measure in the genitive.

reading: and [[in this way|in this way, in this manner, so, thus, even so, so much]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]]; of three hundred [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules]] [[the length|the length, the distances, the height and tallness and stature]] [[of the wooden box|of the wooden box, of the chest, of the coffer]] and of fifty [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules]] [[the breadth|the breadth, the width]] and of thirty [[of fore-arms|of fore-arms, of arms, of centrepieces of the bow, of horns and sides of the lyre, of cubits and ells, of cubit-rules]] [[the height|the height, the top and summit and crown]] of it.

greek: ἐπισυνάγων ποιήσεις τὴν κιβωτὸν καὶ εἰς πῆχυν συντελέσεις αὐτὴν ἄνωθεν· τὴν δὲ θύραν τῆς κιβωτοῦ ποιήσεις ἐκ πλαγίων· κατάγαια, διώροφα καὶ τριώροφα ποιήσεις αὐτήν.
hint: The Hebrew's window, or roof, is not here; the Greek has 'drawing it together'.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ṣōhar taʿăśeh lattēbâ*, *a ṣōhar you shall make for the ark* — a word for a window or a roof, found only here. The Greek has *drawing together you will make the box*, and no opening.
*To a cubit you will finish it from above*, as the Hebrew *wĕʾel-ʾammâ tĕkallennâ milmaʿlâ*.
*From the sides*, plural; the Hebrew *bĕṣiddāh* is *in its side*. πλάγιος as a noun, τὰ πλάγια, is *the sides, the flanks*.

The Hebrew is *taḥtiyyim šĕniyyim ûšĕlišîm*, *lower, second and third* decks. κατάγαιος is *under the earth, underground*, filed under κατάγειος. διώροφος is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ's one sense is *with two roofs or stories*, citing this verse. τριώροφος is *of three stories or floors*. One sense each, so both are plain text.

reading: [[collecting and bringing to|collecting and bringing to, gathering together]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]] and [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[fore-arm|fore-arm, arm, centrepiece of the bow, horn and side of the lyre, cubit and ell, cubit-rule]] [[you will bring quite to an end|you will bring quite to an end, you will complete, you will accomplish, you will make up into the whole and into the number]] it [[from above|from above, from on high, from the upper country, above and on high, from the beginning, by descent, over again and anew]]; [[the door|the door, the folding doors, the gate, the court, the trap-door, the frame of planks and raft, the entrance]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[of the wooden box|of the wooden box, of the chest, of the coffer]] [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of sides|of sides, of flanks]]; [[in the earth|in the earth, under the earth, underground, subterranean]], with two roofs or stories and of three stories or floors [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create]] it.

greek: ἐγὼ δὲ ἰδοὺ ἐπάγω τὸν κατακλυσμὸν ὕδωρ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν καταφθεῖραι πᾶσαν σάρκα, ἐν ᾗ ἐστιν πνεῦμα ζωῆς, ὑποκάτω τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· καὶ ὅσα ἐὰν ᾖ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τελευτήσει.
hint: The deluge is named here, in the word Matthew, Luke and 2 Peter use for it.

notes.text: The Hebrew *hammabbûl mayim*, *the flood, water*, set side by side, and the Greek keeps both. κατακλυσμός, *a deluge, inundation*, is the word of Matthew 24:38–39, Luke 17:27 and 2 Peter 2:5.
The Hebrew *rûaḥ ḥayyîm*. πνεῦμα, lower case, as at 1:2 and 6:3.
τελευτάω is first *to complete, finish, accomplish*; *to end life, to die* is its second sense, which is the verse's. The Hebrew *yigwāʿ* is *will expire*.
ὅσος, *as great as, as many as*, with ἐάν for ἄν: *as many as may be*. Perseus's opening Latin, *quantus*, is left out.

reading: I [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[lo|lo, behold, see there]] [[I bring on|I bring on, I bring upon, I set on and urge on, I lead on, I bring in and invite, I bring to, I lay on and apply, I bring forward, I add]] [[the deluge|the deluge, the inundation]] water [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[to destroy|to destroy, to spoil utterly, to bring to naught]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[flesh|flesh, the flesh, muscles, the body, man's nature generally]], [[in which|within, inside of, and by means of which]] is [[blowing|breath, wind, moving air, respiration, spirit]] [[of a living|of a living, of the means of life and substance, of life and existence, of a way of life]], [[below|below, under]] [[of the heaven|of the heaven, of the vault, of the firmament and the sky]]; and [[as great as|as great as, as much as, as far as, as long as, as many as]] ever may be [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], [[will complete|will complete, will finish, will accomplish, will fulfil, will bring about, will bring to an end, will make an end of, will end life and die, will come to an end]].

greek: καὶ στήσω τὴν διαθήκην μου πρὸς σέ· εἰσελεύσῃ δὲ εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, σὺ καὶ οἱ υἱοί σου καὶ ἡ γυνή σου καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τῶν υἱῶν σου μετὰ σοῦ.
hint: The first διαθήκη in the Bible, a word whose first sense is a will.

notes.text: *Covenant*, Hebrew *bĕrît*. Middle Liddell's first sense is *a disposition of property by will, a will, testament*; *an arrangement between two parties, covenant* is its second. Hebrews 9:16 turns on the first: ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη, θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τοῦ διαθεμένου.
ἵστημι in its causal tenses, *to make to stand, set*. The Hebrew *wahăqimōtî* is also *I will cause to stand*.
πρός with the accusative, *toward* you; the Hebrew *ʾittāk* is *with you*.
μετά with the genitive, the pronoun as plain text, as at 3:6.

reading: and [[I will make to stand|I will make to stand, I will set, I will stop and stay and check, I will set up and raise, I will establish and institute, I will appoint, I will weigh]] [[the disposition|the disposition of property by will, the will and testament, the arrangement between two parties, the covenant]] of me [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] you; [[you will go in|you will go in, you will go into and enter, you will come into, you will come in, you will come upon]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the wooden box|the wooden box, the chest, the coffer]], you and the sons of you and [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse]] of you and [[the women|the women, the mistresses and ladies, the wives and spouses, the mortal women]] of the sons of you [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] you.

greek: καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἑρπετῶν καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν θηρίων καὶ ἀπὸ πάσης σαρκός, δύο δύο ἀπὸ πάντων εἰσάξεις εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, ἵνα τρέφῃς μετὰ σεαυτοῦ· ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἔσονται.
hint: The lexicon's first sense for 'keeping alive' is 'thickening'.

notes.text: *Two two*, a distributive, *two by two*. [[flag]] The Hebrew here is *šnayim mikkōl*, *two of every*; the doubled form is the Hebrew's at 7:9.

[[flag]] The Hebrew is *lĕhaḥăyōt ʾittāk*, *to keep alive with you*. The Greek has τρέφω, whose first sense in Middle Liddell is *to thicken* or *congeal* a liquid, *to curdle* milk; *to make to grow, bring up, rear* is its second, and *to maintain, support* comes later. The headword keeps the lexicon's order.

notes.lemma: ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ … τῶν ἑρπετῶν καὶ … τῶν θηρίων
notes.text: The Hebrew has *from all the living, from all flesh*; the Greek names cattle, creeping things and wild animals before *all flesh*.
The words of 1:27 and 5:2, now of the animals.

greek: ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ὀρνέων τῶν πετεινῶν κατὰ γένος καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν κτηνῶν κατὰ γένος καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἑρπετῶν τῶν ἑρπόντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κατὰ γένος αὐτῶν, δύο δύο ἀπὸ πάντων εἰσελεύσονται πρὸς σὲ τρέφεσθαι μετὰ σοῦ, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ.
hint: The Greek adds 'male and female' again at the end.

notes.text: *According to kind*, the Hebrew *lĕmînô*. γένος is first *race, stock, family*, and *a class, sort, kind* late in the entry.
The present infinitive, middle or passive. Middle Liddell's first gloss for that voice is the passive of *to thicken*, *to become firm*; *to be reared, grow up* follows.
[[flag]] Not in the Hebrew of this verse, which ends *to keep alive*.
Two words for birds: ὄρνεον, *a bird*, and πετεινόν, *winged fowl*. The Hebrew has *hāʿôp* alone, and the Greek adds πάντων before it.

greek: σὺ δὲ λήμψῃ σεαυτῷ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν βρωμάτων, ἃ ἔδεσθε, καὶ συνάξεις πρὸς σεαυτόν, καὶ ἔσται σοὶ καὶ ἐκείνοις φαγεῖν.
hint: Food 'which you will eat', where the Hebrew has 'which is eaten'.

notes.text: *Which you will eat*, the future of ἐσθίω, second person plural. [[flag]] The Hebrew *ʾăšer yēʾākēl* is passive, *which is eaten*.
βρῶμα, *that which is eaten, food, meat*, from the same root as βρῶσις at 2:9.
*For those*: the animals of 6:19–20.

greek: καὶ ἐποίησεν Νωε πάντα, ὅσα ἐνετείλατο αὐτῷ κύριος ὁ θεός, οὕτως ἐποίησεν.
hint: Noah does all that he was commanded.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *ʾĕlōhîm*, *God*; the Greek adds κύριος.
ὅσος, *as great as, as many as*: *all, as many things as*.
